name: Carlsbad structure

plans.label: Minority attack
plans.description: Two queenside pawns advance against three, aiming for b5 and a structural concession on c6.

success.note: A backward Black c-pawn on a file that is half-open for White.

plans.label: Achieve e3-e4
plans.description: Prepare f3 and e3-e4 with a rook behind the e-pawn, and get the pawn to e4 with the d4 pawn still standing.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Central break', whose success was whether the break worked. It is now whether the break was achieved: a White pawn stands on e4 with d4 still behind it. This certifies arrival, not value. Original success note: 'No rules-arithmetic signature distinguishes a working break from a wasted one.'

plans.label: Land h4-h5 against a hook
plans.description: Reroute a knight toward the kingside and play h4-h5 when a hook exists: the pawn reaches h5 while a Black pawn still stands on h6 or g6.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Kingside attack', whose success was whether the attack was sound. It is now whether the lever arrived against a hook: White's pawn on h5 with a Black pawn still on h6 or g6. Overextension looks identical to this census, and the entry says so rather than pretending otherwise. Original success note: 'No rules-arithmetic signature distinguishes attack from overextension.'

plans.label: Reach a queenless position with the c-pawn sound
plans.description: Simplify before the queenside concession can be attacked: get the queens off while the c-pawn is still not a backward target.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Trade pieces', whose success was what the trades were worth. It is now the state the simplification is for: the queens are off and Black's c-pawn is not backward. It counts the two facts, not the bargain. Original success note: 'Detection cannot count what a trade was worth.' Degenerate-case guard: the earlier draft of this signature was vacuously true over an empty piece set, so an existence clause was added. A captured c-pawn also satisfies 'not backward'; the pawn must still be on the board.

plans.label: Get the pawn to a5 with b4 still empty
plans.description: Stop b4 with ...a5, accepting softer queenside squares: the a-pawn stands on a5 and no White pawn has reached b4.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Freeze the queenside', whose success was that b4 never happens — a claim about the future. It is now the present tense of the same thing: Black's pawn stands on a5 and White has no pawn on b4. Original success note: 'The absence of a future advance is not decidable from one position.'

plans.label: Central counter-break
plans.description: Answer wing play in the centre with ...c5, or ...e5 where that pawn survives.

success.note: The c-file tension resolves without leaving White a backward-pawn target.

watch: The attacker and defender count on b5 before the pawn goes there.
Which rook commits to which file.
Whether the c6 pawn still has a pawn neighbour.
typicalMistakes: Switching plans after spending tempi on the first one.
Pushing b5 after a supporting piece moved away.
Playing the central break before it is prepared.
